assertion.statement: There is one integral universal correction eta in O[G] such that the same corrected relaxed coordinate tilde_u=eta*u_rel satisfies tilde_u_x=epsilon_x*u_prim,x at every character, with epsilon_x a Lambda unit. Central valuations and zeros transfer whenever the primitive coordinate is regular.
assertion.objects: Actual primitive-to-relaxed map i and paired strict map j, actual retained classes and their own closed functionals, unused-prime factors e_q=a_q-z-z^(-1), two-place quotient factor l_q, and finite binary groupG.
assertion.hypotheses: The retained norm identity and boundary, cup-pairing naturality and original integral determinant bases are supplied. Every graph prime, including unused ones, has the prescribed scalar exponent. Rational E[2] makes a_q even at good oddq.
assertion.quantifiers: Each unused good split prime and every character of the same finite binary family, with one eta before character evaluation.
assertion.parameter_range: Lambda=Z2[[t]], O its completed localization at(2); good oddq and common graph-wide moving character.
assertion.uniformity: The correction is constructed in the original O[G] for the whole family, without character-by-character interpolation or group-order denominators.
assertion.normalizations: Both the actual class and its own paired functional contribute onee_q. Comparison signs and unit disks give Lambda units, not merelyO units. eta is the product of1+v_q(1+g_q).
assertion.exceptional_cases: eta_x can have a pole at t=0; only its product withu_rel,x is specialized. No integral self-duality of the primitive condition or interpolation ofepsilon_x is assumed.
assertion.limit_order: Use the actual norm boundary and pairing naturality; compare quotient determinants in retained bases; prove e_q is anO[G]unit via reduction t^2/(1+t); construct integralv_q and oneeta; then evaluate characters and transfer regular central data.
